about:
# Bag Steward 0.1.9 — WoW Forever

One financial appraisal for two jobs: choosing a stack to discard when bags fill up, and deciding what to auction, vendor, or disenchant.

## Getting started

Enable **Bag Steward** in the character's AddOns list and log in. A newly installed folder may require restarting WoW rather than reloading.

- **/bstew** or **/bagsteward** — toggle the review window.
- **/bstew options** — settings, also available under Options → AddOns → Bag Steward.
- **/bstew refresh** — discard cached quotes and appraise again.
- **/bstew status** — pricing availability and bag totals.
- **/bstew resetposition** — restore the review window's position.
- **/bstew restore 12345** — remove a manual ignore by item ID.
- Key Bindings → Bag Steward provides review and settings bindings. No bindings are assigned automatically.

A standard **LibDBIcon minimap button** wraps the same LDB entry and is shown by default. Drag it to move it; position is saved per character. Hide it with **Show minimap button** in settings. It works alongside Bazooka and minimap-button collectors. In Bazooka, enable **BagSteward** and its text if it does not appear automatically.

## Broker controls

The LDB text shows the next candidate, its quantity and the modeled loss for the **whole stack**. It does not repeat the free-slot count already available in bag addons. Hover for the first eight candidates. The minimap button shares the same tooltip and click controls.

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Left-click | Toggle the review window |
| Shift-left-click | Drop the current candidate, with confirmation by default |
| Right-click | Settings |
| Ctrl-right-click | Keep that item on this character |
| Ctrl-left-click | Sell the candidate at an open vendor, with confirmation by default |

Review rows share the broker's modifiers:

| Input on a row | Action |
|---|---|
| Left-click | Select |
| Right-click | Item actions: Details, Keep / Stop keeping, Sell, Drop, Search AH |
| Ctrl-right-click | Keep this item |
| Ctrl-left-click | Sell this stack at an open vendor |
| Shift-left-click | Drop this stack |

Selling and dropping use the same confirmation and live stack/quest checks as before. Protected actions are disabled in the menu. A menu retains the named stack's identity through list refreshes. A right-click menu on a kept item provides **Stop keeping**, including for keeps not currently carried. The **Kept items** dropdown filter only changes the view; it does not mark an item.

Manual keeps apply to every copy of that item ID on the current character. They survive filter changes, rescans, bag moves, reacquiring an item and reloads. Kept items stay out of Vendor/AH/DE and discard suggestions, and cannot be sold or destroyed through Bag Steward until released. The **Kept items** filter can release keeps even when no copies are currently carried. Existing manual ignores are preserved as keeps in the same saved-variable field.

## Bags full

The loot helper appears below the loot frame when looting with full general bags. It offers Drop, Keep and Review. It disappears when looting ends or space becomes available. A specialty bag's free slots do not count as room for ordinary loot. When general bags are full, items in general bags rank ahead of specialty-bag items.

**Quest items and needed turn-in quantities are protected by default.** Protection uses the native quest log and bag flags, Quest item category, quest binding, QuestieDB's public quest-objective data, and quest-linked collection/turn-in steps in the currently loaded RXP guide.

Ordinary items such as Murloc Eyes or cooking meats can therefore appear as **Keep** even though their item type is food or trade goods. Right-click a row → **Details** to see the quest name, source, needed quantity and carried quantity. A finished collection objective stays reserved until hand-in. Completed quests and obsolete guide-only needs are released when their source updates; no permanent manual keep is created.

Requirements for the same item in different quests are added together. Multiple sources describing the same quest are deduplicated. A whole stack is eligible only if enough carried items remain after its removal. If a stack mixes required and excess items, it stays protected as a whole; split the excess manually. Requirements and live carried counts are checked again at the click/confirmation so two actions cannot both consume the same reserve.

Native Quest-category/bound items and quest starters remain protected regardless of surplus. Required source items without a published quantity are protected conservatively. Protection uses **Ignore quest items**; manual keeps remain a separate preference.

Scope: active quests, plus linked needs found in the **currently loaded RXP guide**. RXP completed collect steps are not mistaken for completed hand-ins. QuestieDB supplies quantities for active quests and RXP's upcoming hand-ins, rather than blacklisting every item ever used by any quest. Unlinked shopping lists and profession-leveling collections are not automatically treated as turn-in reserves. Unloaded chapters, guide prose without structured item/quest links, and missing database records can require a manual Keep.

Questie readiness/quest updates and native quest events trigger refreshes. A lightweight poll detects RXP guide/step changes. The read-only RXP adapter uses the installed v4.11.35 guide structure; future RXP changes may require an adapter update. Optional addons can be absent; native quest-log protection remains. **/bstew status** reports the available sources.

**Profession tools are also protected by default**, with a separate **Ignore profession tools** checkbox. Mining picks, skinning knives, blacksmith hammers, engineering tools, runed enchanting rods, alchemy tools, Flint and Tinder, fishing poles and the known Forever tool variants appear as Keep. Drop/sell actions are blocked while protection is on. Raw rods, vials, consumed wood and other crafting materials are not treated as reusable tools. This uses known tool IDs and item categories, not English name matching; custom items outside those known categories/IDs may need a manual ignore.

Food, drink, potions, soulbound items and items with no vendor price remain eligible unless manually ignored or covered by quest/tool protection. Unknown values remain visible and sort after known values; an unknown value is not silently treated as zero.

Each drop frees one occupied slot by destroying the whole stack. The selection is checked again after confirmation. A different link, quantity or GUID, a locked stack, occupied cursor or combat blocks the action. Without a GUID, any intervening bag update blocks the pending action.

## Vendor and AH review

The same movable review window opens at vendors and the auction house by default. These are independent settings.

The review window starts **compact: 430 × 350 UI units, seven rows**, with Item and Value per stack. A small **A/V/D/K/? badge on the item icon** conveys its route. There is no separate route column or bottom action-button row. Text size is unchanged. Value follows the recommendation (vendor return, expected AH net, or expected DE net).

**Hover shows the standard item tooltip**, using the actual carried bag slot so normal tooltip addons can contribute. For moved items or saved keeps not currently carried, it falls back to the item's link or ID. No Bag Steward appraisal lines are appended.

**Right-click → Details** opens the appraisal separately in a scrollable, read-only panel: prices, sources, fees, chance assumptions, time costs, quest reserves and the recommendation's explanation. It opens only when requested and retains a snapshot until reopened; hover never opens it.

A standard WoW dropdown selects **All / Vendor / AH / DE / Kept items / Review**. The **...** menu contains Refresh prices and Settings. **Expand** restores the comparison columns and twelve rows in a 1010 × 520 frame; **Compact** shrinks it again. The choice is remembered per character, along with the movable window position. Pagination and mouse-wheel paging work in both sizes.

- At a **vendor**, the **Vendor filter** is selected automatically and only vendor recommendations appear. Ctrl-left-click a row, or right-click → **Sell stack**, to sell that one stack with confirmation.
- At the **AH**, the **AH filter** is selected automatically. Right-click a row → **Search AH** launches an exact-name Auctionator search.
- Manual review outside those contexts opens **All**. You can explicitly choose All or another filter during a visit; scans preserve that choice. A new visit selects the relevant context filter again. The native dropdown shows the active filter. Changing filters clears the previous selection.
- Protected quest items and profession tools appear in Kept items with an explanation.
- Right-click a row → **Details** for raw prices, expected returns, sources, uncertainty, deposit assumptions, sale probability and time costs.

No automatic selling, deleting, posting or disenchanting. AH posting and disenchanting remain manual in version 0.1. Economic advice does not determine whether an item is an upgrade, crafting reagent or something you personally want.

## Baganator

A corner widget displays **A** (auction), **V** (vendor), **D** (disenchant), **K** (manual keep), or **?** (review). Registered through Baganator's public corner-widget API, enabled at the top-left by default. Change the corner in Baganator, or switch marks off in Bag Steward.

Marks apply to live carried items on this character. Bank and other-character items are not guessed from item ID. This addon does **not** register a junk provider, change Baganator's existing junk provider or classify the financial recommendations as auto-sell junk. KeepOrToss can still provide its separate quest/crafting-use context.

## Pricing and the model

All amounts are copper internally and stack totals in the review window.

Sources:

1. Auctionator scan price when its scan age is known and at most three days old.
2. TSM DBRecent / DBMarket, converted through the public ToItemString API. Their age is not exposed here and is labeled unknown.
3. Older or age-unknown Auctionator quotes, then TSM regional-sale/historical fallback.
4. Vendor-only appraisal if market data is unavailable.

The model allows 100% of a fresh Auctionator quote, 80% of an age-unknown TSM local quote, or 60% of a fallback quote. An observed quote above twice the regional-sale/historical reference is capped **only for modeling**, with the raw quote still shown. These are conservative estimates, not measured confidence intervals.

TSM's regional sale rate is used as a *per-listing proxy*. Without it, the assumed chance is 35% per listing. Two listings are allowed by default. If neither sells, the model credits the vendor fallback:

    expected AH net =
        probability of eventual sale × allowed quote × (1 − AH cut)
        + probability of no sale × vendor return
        − expected failed listings × deposit
        − listing time cost − bag holding cost

A deposit is refunded on success; it is charged as a cost only when the modeled listing fails. At the AH, the game deposit API is tried using the actual item location/count and selected duration. Otherwise, the displayed estimate is the greater of a configurable 1s floor or 15% / 30% / 60% of vendor value for 12h / 24h / 48h. This fallback is an assumption, not a claim about current server rules. A valid game deposit of zero stays zero. The default AH cut is 5%; configure it if your market differs.

Default hourly time value is **600 + 8 × (level − 1)² copper** (about 29s/hour at level 18). This is adjustable, not observed income. Handling takes 15 modeled seconds per listing. At 75–100% general-bag occupancy, an extra holding penalty grows from zero to two minutes of that hourly value.

AH must beat vendor by at least **1s or 25% of vendor value**, whichever is greater. That hurdle grows up to threefold under bag pressure. An unaffordable deposit blocks an AH recommendation. Settings expose the time value, hurdle, sale-rate fallback, attempts, duration, AH cut, deposit floor and acceptable scan age.

For gear, Auctionator's expected disenchant value is preferred, with TSM **destroy** as fallback. DE net uses an 85% materials realization allowance, the assumed AH cut and five seconds per cast. Materials price age is unknown. DE recommendations require Disenchant to be known, but **per-item eligibility and skill requirements still need checking in game**. No claim is made that every green/blue can actually be disenchanted.

The discard score is the greatest modeled realizable return from vendor, AH or DE, for the whole stack. It is an economic opportunity-cost estimate, not a replacement for checking personal use.

## Validation and limits

Lua 5.1 syntax checked; behavior executed with Fengari and mocked WoW APIs, including the actual embedded LDB and LibDBIcon libraries. Tests cover valuation, missing/stale data, full general versus specialty bags, quest/tool protection, turn-in reserves and surplus, completed collections awaiting hand-in, RXP/QuestieDB deduplication and shared quest items, provider notifications, UI Keep → All → Vendor behavior, keep persistence through saved-variable serialization/reinitialization, compact LDB text, minimap controls/position, Baganator marks, vendor/AH contexts, public price APIs and action revalidation. Keeping an item also blocks previously opened sale/destruction confirmations for it.

**Client appearance and live vendor/auction interactions need checking in game.** Check /bstew, visit a vendor and an AH, then verify the letters and appraisal math in Details against a few known items. Native tooltip routing, unchanged item identity, explicit details opening and preserved appraisal text are covered by offline checks. Actions are opt-in clicks and confirmed by default.

TSM/Auctionator may still have missing, stale or unrealistic data. Recommendations should be read with their quoted source and assumptions. An API failure falls back to the remaining data instead of inventing a market value.

## Local installation / removal

Copy the **BagSteward** folder into the Forever client's **Interface/AddOns** folder. Do not nest it twice. This addon does not modify other addons or their settings. If DropTheCheapestThing is installed again, disable its broker/helper to avoid duplicate discard controls.

To undo, disable Bag Steward in AddOns; no other addon needs restoring. Removing its folder removes the code. Its independent BagStewardDB and per-character BagStewardCharDB saved variables may be retained.

## Components and attribution

Original Bag Steward files are provided under the MIT license in LICENSE.txt. Embedded libraries retain their upstream ownership:

- LibStub: public domain; credits in its source header. https://www.wowace.com/projects/libstub
- CallbackHandler-1.0: Ace3 Development Team; accompanying Ace3 license retained. https://www.wowace.com/projects/callbackhandler
- LibDataBroker-1.1: tekkub and contributors, retained unmodified as an embedded library. Upstream embedding instructions: https://www.wowace.com/projects/libdatabroker-1-1 ; source/API: https://github.com/tekkub/libdatabroker-1-1
- LibDBIcon-1.0: Funkeh, nebula169 and contributors; embedded unmodified, Ace3 Style BSD license. https://www.wowace.com/projects/libdbicon-1-0

No addon-specific code is copied from KeepOrToss or DropTheCheapestThing. Standard libraries were copied unmodified from installed distributions. Integrations use the public TSM, Auctionator, Baganator and QuestieDB APIs, plus native quest data and a read-only RXP guide adapter. No quest database or guide content is redistributed.

releases.notes:
## 0.1.9

- Fixed startup XML warnings in WoW Forever. The game loads Bag Steward's two keybinds automatically and shows them under Bag Steward.

## 0.1.8

First public release for World of Warcraft: Forever.

- Appraise bag stacks for auction, vendor, disenchant, or discard using available Auctionator and TradeSkillMaster prices.
- Review recommendations at a vendor or auction house, in Baganator, or through the DataBroker and minimap button.
- Protect quest turn-ins, profession tools, and items marked Keep. Selling and dropping require a click and prompt for confirmation by default.
- Show the standard item tooltip on hover. Open Details for price sources, estimates, and quest reserves.
